clue.text: Despairing comment when tax breaks end in August

indicators.note: the two words are broken up and their letters reassembled in a new order
the end of the word August supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone groans at the news that a tax break expires in August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns WHEN and TAX into WHATNEX; 'end in August' adds its last letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: An exasperated exclamation on hearing yet another piece of bad news, said in despair.

clue.text: Husband breaking leg used to get delayed

indicators.note: the husband's letter breaks into the run of the other two pieces, splitting them

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side, giving ON
used things are old, second-hand

explanation.surface: A husband with a broken leg has to put his plans off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the 'on' side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postponed or paused, like a phone call waiting, is said to be in a suspended state.

clue.text: Agent's skill in wind with boat

parts.note: a trade wind is a steady tropical wind, so trade can stand for wind
a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor's skill in handling a sailing boat in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage technique is the professional know-how of a spy or secret agent.

clue.text: A host of couples beginning to act in drama

indicators.note: the starting letter is placed inside the Japanese drama

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: the first letter of act is taken

explanation.surface: A party host welcomes couples arriving for the opening of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: NOH is classical Japanese theatre, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ark builder took in the animals two by two, so he hosted a great many pairs.

clue.text: Bona fide ex food manufacturing traveller's description?

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new out of raw material, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A genuine former food producer is described as being on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturing' rearranges BONA FIDE EX FOOD; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone homeless with no permanent address, as a wanderer or itinerant has.

clue.text: Had string of diamonds one's wearing supervised?

indicators.note: the string of diamonds has one inside it, as if worn

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, so a string of them is several Ds
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'
to supervise is to lead

explanation.surface: Someone wore a necklace of diamonds while overseeing others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'one is': I is wearing three Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is slang for being cheated or conned, which matches swindled.

clue.text: Bypass not going around English town

parts.note: to skip something is to bypass it

indicators.note: the word not turns round, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A ring road that fails to go round an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIPTON is a market town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in North Yorkshire, England, known as a gateway to the Dales.

clue.text: Rustic has those for broadening mind

indicators.note: the insertion makes the word for mind wider, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to mind is to heed
the ayes are those in favour in a vote; AYS is an accepted spelling

explanation.surface: A countryman owns things meant to widen one's outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. AYS (ayes) are those voting for.
explanation.definitionFit: A country bumpkin or yokel, an unsophisticated rural person in American slang.

clue.text: One who'd escape the writer's miserable literary confines

indicators.note: the gloomy word encloses the writer, holding them inside

parts.note: drear is a literary word for dreary or miserable
the writer refers to themself as me; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An author resents being trapped in a gloomy literary world.
explanation.walkthrough: DREAR is a poetic form of 'dreary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in fantasy or daydreams escapes from reality in their imagination.

clue.text: Where imposing construction carries sound, ultimately?

definitions.text: Where imposing construction carries sound, ultimately?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the last letter of sound inside them
the two words are built into a new structure of letters
ultimately takes the last letter of the word sound

explanation.surface: A question about which grand building lets sound travel furthest.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a cryptic definition, tempting solvers toward a gallery or wall; 'construction' and 'carries' show it is an anagram with the final letter of 'sound' tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola whose curved shape carries a quiet voice right round its walls to a distant listener, as at St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Push from United not in vain

indicators.note: the abbreviation for United is not included, so it is removed

parts.note: a vain person is proud
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A shove comes from a United player who isn't conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke or nudge someone is to push them, physically or into action.

clue.text: Wind up backing broadcast making allowance for its music?

parts.note: to wind someone up is to needle or annoy them

indicators.note: the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to emit it

explanation.surface: Teasing a radio station by reversing its broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word. 'Wind up' is the British sense of tease.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the quota of airtime a radio station may give to playing recorded discs, under licensing rules.

clue.text: One unlikely to give up lead after overtaking you once

indicators.note: the lead swallows the old word for you, taking it inside

parts.note: the lead in a show is its star
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A runner gives up the lead after being overtaken.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is archaic 'you', hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or athlete with great stamina keeps going over long distances and does not quit.

clue.text: Pour ale all round insect

indicators.note: the drink surrounds the insect, wrapping right round it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone pours beer around a drowning insect.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, to 'be mother' is to pour out the tea for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: the person who pours the tea for the group is said to take on the parent's role.

clue.text: Town's attraction, gripping many times over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the result is turned upside down, read backwards
the attraction holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a draw is an attraction that pulls in a crowd
oft is an old word for often, many times

explanation.surface: A town's main attraction holds visitors many times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts OFT in DRAW, making DROFTAW; 'over' reverses it. WATFORD is a town north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large town in Hertfordshire, just north-west of London, with a well-known football club.

clue.text: One has few bright moments, save for this?

definitions.meaning: a dull, wet day with little sunshine
the saying is to put money by against hard times ahead

explanation.definitionFit: A wet day is literally gloomy, and figuratively it stands for a future time of need.

clue.text: End fuel recycling as required

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: Recycling used fuel is something we must do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something necessary or needed is what the situation calls for.

clue.text: Copied index — or excerpts from floor shows

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards from the bottom
the words show the answer within them

explanation.surface: An index and extracts from floor shows were photocopied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' signals letters within 'inDEX OR EXcerpts'; 'from floor' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a photocopier brand, the verb means duplicated by photocopying.

clue.text: Reveal sponsor: certainly not one from the City

definitions.text: certainly not one from the City

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
a backer is a sponsor or financial supporter

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposes the identity of a sponsor who is no City financier.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'City' is London's financial district, but the definition plays on city versus bush: an Australian from the remote interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Australia's remote interior bush is about as far from urban life as one can get.

clue.text: Ring across enclosed pen

indicators.note: the ring lies across the other piece, around it

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
enc is the abbreviation for enclosed, as on a letter

explanation.surface: A ring is placed over an enclosed pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure or hutch for keeping poultry is a pen for birds.

clue.text: Give up holiday to work

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
to go is to function or work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their holiday plans to go to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To release your grip on something is to relinquish it, a colloquial phrase.

clue.text: Reportedly India's top batsman a revelation

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the letter is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's is 'is'
an opener is one of the first two batsmen in a cricket innings

explanation.surface: India's leading batsman is said to have been a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers bat first, at the top of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising that shows you a truth is said to make you see clearly, a startling discovery.

clue.text: Grave, awfully shy one, nothing like this?

definitions.text: Grave, awfully shy one, nothing like this?

parts.note: a grave is a tomb
nothing is O, zero

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A serious, very timid girl is nothing like a lively boisterous one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges SHY + I + O. The whole clue describes a solemn timid girl, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl who behaves in a boisterous boyish way is the opposite of grave and shy.

clue.text: Answer couple with consecutive letters, most pessimistically

parts.note: a couple is two
R, S and T follow one another in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A pair answer with letters in sequence, expecting the worst.
explanation.definitionFit: If the worst happens, i.e. on the gloomiest view, this phrase gives the outcome.

clue.text: Hip surgeon maybe in spot: something to do with washing

indicators.note: the fashionable and medical pieces go inside the word for spot

parts.note: to spot something is to spy it
hip means fashionable, in
a surgeon is a doctor, abbreviated DR

explanation.surface: A trendy surgeon is caught in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks a surgeon as one example of a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirling clothes in a drum to remove water is a stage of the laundry process.

clue.text: Snake left in den after cutting tail off

indicators.note: the snake and the left go inside the shortened den
the den has its last letter cut away

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road does

explanation.surface: A snake is left in its lair after its tail is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' wants to be the definition, but it is a verb meaning twist; 'tail off' at the end is the definition. 'after cutting' drops the last letter of the lair.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or diminish gradually is to fade away to almost nothing.

clue.text: Artist regularly selected teal, grey and green

indicators.note: every other letter of teal is selected, the 2nd and 4th

parts.note: eco means environmentally green

explanation.surface: A painter carefully picks out teal, grey and green from his palette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly selected' takes E and L from tEaL. El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of Renaissance Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, famous for elongated figures.

clue.text: Some wildlife series, much loved, on radio

indicators.note: on radio signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a row is a series, and dear means much loved

explanation.surface: A much-loved wildlife series broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A row (series) and dear (much loved) are said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A small woodland deer native to Europe is one kind of wildlife among many.
